question_stem:
Fig. 8.1 shows a circuit that produces rectification of an alternating input voltage.

{{figure:9702_s25_42_q08_figure_8_1}}

Fig. 8.1

The input voltage $V_{IN}$ is sinusoidal. The rectified output voltage $V_{OUT}$ is applied across resistor $R$.

The variation of $V_{IN}$ with time $t$ has amplitude $V_0$ and period $T$, as shown in Fig. 8.2.

{{figure:9702_s25_42_q08_figure_8_2}}

Fig. 8.2

The root-mean-square (r.m.s.) value of $V_{IN}$ is $6.0\text{ V}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the type of rectification produced by the circuit of Fig. 8.1.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Resistor $R$ has resistance $45\ \Omega$.

Assume that there is no p.d. across the diode when it is conducting.
parts.text: Determine the peak power $P_0$ in the resistor.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
(b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the answer in (b)(ii) to explain why the mean power in the resistor is $\frac{1}{4}P_0$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(iii) to determine the r.m.s. value of $V_{OUT}$.
